bug_semantics: The global CanInstall middleware recognizes completed installation, but the vulnerable guard redirects only when the request is not AJAX. An attacker can send an AJAX-marked request directly to an install/api route after installation; the request falls through to InstallerController. For admin-config-setup, attacker-controlled administrator fields are hashed/assembled and written to the admins table, enabling administrative account replacement or creation without authentication. The same route group exposes migration, seeding, sample-data, and environment operations. The 2.3.10 fix keeps the installed-state check for AJAX requests and terminates them with HTTP 403.
flaw_origin: The smallest public first-write candidate is e050c9d66656ae50fe208f4ce0a91c2f5956c77d: its one-line CanInstall hunk adds && ! $request->ajax() to a parent guard that previously blocked every already-installed /install request. The sole parent ce555ac4c5dced0f882b2508d2016e811d5a978a already has the installer API and admin-config route but not the bypass. The candidate and parent are absent from the assigned clone, so their SHA fields are withheld rather than violating the clone-object contract.
